closest_bound_comparison.source: Zofia Stemplowska, Duties to the Dead: Is Posthumous Mitigation of Injustice Possible? (2020), accepted manuscript §§2.2–4.3 and conclusion; read in full.
closest_bound_comparison.overlap: Both concern whether justice can require a remedy after the victim dies without relying on posthumous well-being.
closest_bound_comparison.difference: Stemplowska's argument turns on advancing surviving preferences/projects and on limits for permissible mitigation. The candidate proposes a time-indexed remedial liability and continuing institutional endorsement, without making a surviving preference the ground.
closest_bound_comparison.significance: This is a real difference in proposed grounding, but it neither proves that the candidate's route is original nor establishes that it works. Stemplowska also brackets some status-affirming considerations; that omission is not a novelty result.
